newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-BASF promises more strong results in 97.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BASF promises more strong results in 97.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group BASF AG on Thursday promised shareholders another good year as first quarter 1997 results showed business got off to a strong start.

Reporting a 13.6 percent rise in sales and a 3.2 percent increase in net profits in the first quarter, management board chairman Juergen Strube repeated an earlier forecast for full year sales to top 50 billion marks ($29.5 billion) and profits to be good.
"Our order books are well filled and we stand a good chance to enjoy another special year," Strube told shareholders, echoing statements made at a news conference one month ago.
"Our dividend payments will continue to be based on our results," Strube, well-known for downplaying forecasts, added.
BASF will pay a 1.70 marks per share dividend for 1996.
Shares closed 0.2 percent lower at 67.28 in high volume trade while the broader DAX index closed down 0.32 percent at 3,562.11 points.
Breaking down its results, BASF said "an overall virgorous rise in volumes and a considerable expansion of the oil and gas segment with improved prices were the mainstays of the increase in sales."
The group posted a 10.7 percent rise in domestic sales and an 14.7 percent increase in foreign sales with North American sales posting the single highest increase.
Sales there climbed 22 percent to 2.8 billion marks. In Europe, still BASF's largest market, sales climbed 11 percent to 9.6 billion marks.

Nonetheless, BASF faced higher raw materials prices which forced production costs to rise somewhat more sharply than sales. Personnel costs rose by 5.7 percent, with two percentage points coming from personnel costs in North America, which were affected by the dollar conversion rate.

The company also said fiancial results declined to 3.0 million marks from 54 million marks during the first quarter of 1996. BASF said interest results did not match the previous year's figure due to a reduction in cash and cash items.
BASF also said it planned to increase sales in its drugs division through internal growth not through further acquisitions.

"To achieve this we are betting on new products," BASF management board member Gerhard Wolf said, adding the group had promising products to treat obesity, pain and schizophrenia. BASF said it was expecting the largest gain from the obesity drug Meridia.
On the other hand, Wolf also said: "We don't rule out acquisitions but they must fit with us strategically."
Analysts have said that BASF would be in a position to make more purchases and should do so in order to keep pace with fast-moving consolidation in the pharmaceuticals industry.
BASF said the income from operations in the health and nutrition sector stood at 325 million marks in the first quarter, down 12 million marks from year ago levels.
